entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Heinrich Schütz was a German early Baroque composer and organist, generally regarded as the most important German composer before Johann Sebastian Bach and one of the most important composers of the 17th century. He is credited with bringing the Italian style to Germany and continuing its evolution from the Renaissance into the early Baroque. Most of his surviving music was written for the Lutheran church, primarily for the Electoral Chapel in Dresden. He wrote what is traditionally considered the first German opera, Dafne, performed at Torgau in 1627, the music of which has since been lost, along with nearly all of his ceremonial and theatrical scores.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Heinrich Schütz's contributions to German music and opera had a significant regional impact, shaping the development of Baroque music in Germany and influencing later composers such as Bach. His work on ceremonial and theatrical scores helped establish the Lutheran church's musical traditions.
